query: SELECT title FROM books b WHERE b.id IN (SELECT l.book_id FROM loans l WHERE l.status = 'overdue');
gold_checklist: Must say: title of books whose id appears among the book_id values in loans where loan status is 'overdue'. Must reflect this is a membership check against a filtered list, not a join returning loans columns.

query: SELECT en.id, en.credits, SUM(en.credits) OVER (ORDER BY en.semester_date) AS running_total FROM enrollments en;
gold_checklist: Must say: a running (cumulative) total of credits in course enrollments, ordered by semester_date, where each row's total includes all prior rows' amounts plus its own — not the sum for the whole table on every row.

query: SELECT name, CASE WHEN age > 100 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS tier FROM patients;
gold_checklist: Must say: labels each row of patients as 'high' if its age is above 100, and 'low' otherwise (100 itself falls into 'low' since the condition is strictly greater-than).

query: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', hire_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS n FROM employees GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
gold_checklist: Must say: number of employees rows per calendar month based on hire_date, ordered chronologically. Must not describe this as per-day, per-year, or unordered.

query: SELECT p.id, p.age, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.city ORDER BY p.age DESC) AS rnk FROM patients p;
gold_checklist: Must say: ranks patients by age WITHIN each city group (not company/table-wide), highest age = rank 1 in each group. Must explicitly mention the per-city partitioning.

query: SELECT b.title, a.name FROM books b JOIN loans l ON b.id = l.book_id JOIN authors a ON l.id = a.id;
gold_checklist: Must say: connects books, loans, and authors through two matches, returning title paired with the related name from authors. Must reflect that a row only appears if matches exist in all three tables.

query: SELECT AVG(balance) AS average_balance FROM accounts;
gold_checklist: Must say: the average balance across all rows of accounts — a single number, not a per-row or per-group result.

query: SELECT name, age FROM patients WHERE city = 'Tunis';
gold_checklist: Must say: returns the name and age of patients where city equals 'Tunis'. Must not mention any other filter or column.

query: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE email > (SELECT AVG(email) FROM customers);
gold_checklist: Must say: name of customers whose email is above the average email of ALL customers. Must reflect the average is computed across the whole table, not a filtered subset.

query: SELECT a1.name AS person, a2.name AS related_person FROM patients a1 JOIN patients a2 ON a1.id = a2.id - 1;
gold_checklist: Must say: pairs each row of patients with the row whose id is exactly one less, showing both names side by side (a self-join, comparing patients against itself, not against a different table).

query: SELECT AVG(price) AS average_price FROM books;
gold_checklist: Must say: the average price across all rows of books — a single number, not a per-row or per-group result.

query: SELECT a.owner_name, t.id FROM accounts a RIGHT JOIN transactions t ON a.id = t.account_id;
gold_checklist: Must say: every row from transactions is kept, with owner_name from accounts filled in if there's a match, or blank if the accounts row is missing. Must correctly identify that this preserves transactions rows even without a match (RIGHT JOIN), not the reverse.

query: SELECT t.id, t.amount, SUM(t.amount) OVER (ORDER BY t.transaction_date) AS running_total FROM transactions t;
gold_checklist: Must say: a running (cumulative) total of amount in transactions, ordered by transaction_date, where each row's total includes all prior rows' amounts plus its own — not the sum for the whole table on every row.

query: SELECT name FROM employees e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM departments d WHERE d.department_id = e.id);
gold_checklist: Must say: name of employees that have at least one related row in departments. Must not describe this as returning combined columns from both tables — EXISTS only checks presence, it doesn't pull data from departments.

query: SELECT * FROM patients ORDER BY registered_date DESC LIMIT 5;
gold_checklist: Must say: the 5 most recent patients by registered_date, all columns, newest first. Must mention both the limit of 5 and the descending order.

query: SELECT p.name, ap.id FROM patients p INNER JOIN appointments ap ON p.id = ap.patient_id;
gold_checklist: Must say: name from patients paired with the id of each matching appointments row, for patients that have at least one related appointments row. Must note that patients with NO matching appointments are excluded (INNER JOIN behavior).

query: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY gpa DESC) AS overall_rank FROM students;
gold_checklist: Must say: ranks ALL of students by GPA across the whole table (no grouping/partitioning), highest = rank 1, no ties share a rank (each row gets a unique number, unlike RANK()).

query: SELECT ap.id, ap.cost, SUM(ap.cost) OVER (ORDER BY ap.appointment_date) AS running_total FROM appointments ap;
gold_checklist: Must say: a running (cumulative) total of cost in appointments, ordered by appointment_date, where each row's total includes all prior rows' amounts plus its own — not the sum for the whole table on every row.

query: SELECT s.name, en.id FROM students s LEFT JOIN enrollments en ON s.id = en.student_id;
gold_checklist: Must say: every row from students is included, with the matching course enrollments id if one exists, or blank/null if not. Must NOT say students without a match are excluded — that would be INNER JOIN behavior, not LEFT JOIN.

query: SELECT AVG(salary) AS average_salary FROM employees;
gold_checklist: Must say: the average salary across all rows of employees — a single number, not a per-row or per-group result.

query: SELECT ap.patient_id, SUM(ap.cost) AS total FROM appointments ap GROUP BY ap.patient_id HAVING SUM(ap.cost) > 1000;
gold_checklist: Must say: total cost per patient_id in appointments, only including groups whose total exceeds 1000. Must mention the HAVING threshold as a filter applied AFTER grouping/summing, separate from any row-level filter.

query: SELECT t.account_id, SUM(t.amount) AS total FROM transactions t GROUP BY t.account_id HAVING SUM(t.amount) > 1000;
gold_checklist: Must say: total amount per account_id in transactions, only including groups whose total exceeds 1000. Must mention the HAVING threshold as a filter applied AFTER grouping/summing, separate from any row-level filter.

query: SELECT name, CASE WHEN gpa > 100 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS tier FROM students;
gold_checklist: Must say: labels each row of students as 'high' if its GPA is above 100, and 'low' otherwise (100 itself falls into 'low' since the condition is strictly greater-than).

query: SELECT c.name, o.amount FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'shipped';
gold_checklist: Must say: name and amount for matched customers/orders pairs, restricted to rows where status is 'shipped'. Must mention BOTH the join match requirement and the status filter as separate conditions.

query: SELECT e.name, d.id FROM employees e LEFT JOIN departments d ON e.id = d.department_id;
gold_checklist: Must say: every row from employees is included, with the matching departments id if one exists, or blank/null if not. Must NOT say employees without a match are excluded — that would be INNER JOIN behavior, not LEFT JOIN.

query: SELECT c.name, p.name FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id JOIN products p ON o.id = p.id;
gold_checklist: Must say: connects customers, orders, and products through two matches, returning name paired with the related name from products. Must reflect that a row only appears if matches exist in all three tables.

query: SELECT name, gpa FROM students WHERE major = 'Computer Science';
gold_checklist: Must say: returns the name and GPA of students where major equals 'Computer Science'. Must not mention any other filter or column.

query: WITH big_spenders AS (SELECT student_id, SUM(credits) AS total FROM enrollments GROUP BY student_id HAVING SUM(credits) > 1000) SELECT s.name, bs.total FROM students s JOIN big_spenders bs ON s.id = bs.student_id;
gold_checklist: Must say: first computes, per student_id, the total credits in course enrollments and keeps only totals above 1000 (the CTE), then joins that back to students to show name alongside each qualifying total. Must reflect both stages: the aggregation/threshold step and the join step.

query: SELECT name FROM students WHERE major = 'Computer Science' UNION SELECT co.title FROM courses co WHERE co.department = 'Computer Science';
gold_checklist: Must say: combines name values from students matching major='Computer Science' with title values from courses matching the same filter, into one list with duplicates removed (UNION drops duplicates; UNION ALL would keep them).

query: SELECT p.name, ap.cost FROM patients p INNER JOIN appointments ap ON p.id = ap.patient_id WHERE ap.status = 'completed';
gold_checklist: Must say: name and cost for matched patients/appointments pairs, restricted to rows where appointment status is 'completed'. Must mention BOTH the join match requirement and the status filter as separate conditions.

query: SELECT a1.name AS person, a2.name AS related_person FROM students a1 JOIN students a2 ON a1.id = a2.id - 1;
gold_checklist: Must say: pairs each row of students with the row whose id is exactly one less, showing both names side by side (a self-join, comparing students against itself, not against a different table).

query: SELECT e.name, pr.name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.id = d.department_id JOIN projects pr ON d.id = pr.id;
gold_checklist: Must say: connects employees, departments, and projects through two matches, returning name paired with the related name from projects. Must reflect that a row only appears if matches exist in all three tables.

query: SELECT name FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id);
gold_checklist: Must say: name of customers that have NO related row in orders at all. Must not confuse this with 'not the most recent' or any other partial condition — it means zero matches.

query: SELECT account_type, COUNT(*) AS total FROM accounts GROUP BY account_type;
gold_checklist: Must say: the number of accounts rows for each distinct account type. Must mention that this is a count per group, not a total across all accounts.

query: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE country = 'Tunisia' UNION SELECT p.name FROM products p WHERE p.category = 'Tunisia';
gold_checklist: Must say: combines name values from customers matching country='Tunisia' with name values from products matching the same filter, into one list with duplicates removed (UNION drops duplicates; UNION ALL would keep them).

query: SELECT en.student_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrollments en GROUP BY en.student_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;
gold_checklist: Must say: student_id values that appear in at least 3 rows of course enrollments, along with that count. Must reflect that this filters on the count of rows per group, not on any individual row's value.

query: SELECT c.name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS related_count FROM customers c;
gold_checklist: Must say: for every row in customers, shows name plus a count of how many rows in orders reference it (0 if none). Must mention this includes customers with zero matches, showing 0 rather than excluding them (unlike an INNER JOIN would).

query: SELECT a1.owner_name AS person, a2.owner_name AS related_person FROM accounts a1 JOIN accounts a2 ON a1.id = a2.id - 1;
gold_checklist: Must say: pairs each row of accounts with the row whose id is exactly one less, showing both owner_names side by side (a self-join, comparing accounts against itself, not against a different table).

query: SELECT t.account_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM transactions t GROUP BY t.account_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3;
gold_checklist: Must say: account_id values that appear in at least 3 rows of transactions, along with that count. Must reflect that this filters on the count of rows per group, not on any individual row's value.

query: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', signup_date) AS month, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
gold_checklist: Must say: number of customers rows per calendar month based on signup_date, ordered chronologically. Must not describe this as per-day, per-year, or unordered.

query: SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(o.amount) AS total FROM orders o GROUP BY o.customer_id HAVING SUM(o.amount) > 1000;
gold_checklist: Must say: total amount per customer_id in orders, only including groups whose total exceeds 1000. Must mention the HAVING threshold as a filter applied AFTER grouping/summing, separate from any row-level filter.

query: SELECT s.name, en.id FROM students s RIGHT JOIN enrollments en ON s.id = en.student_id;
gold_checklist: Must say: every row from course enrollments is kept, with name from students filled in if there's a match, or blank if the students row is missing. Must correctly identify that this preserves course enrollments rows even without a match (RIGHT JOIN), not the reverse.

query: SELECT p.name, ap.id FROM patients p RIGHT JOIN appointments ap ON p.id = ap.patient_id;
gold_checklist: Must say: every row from appointments is kept, with name from patients filled in if there's a match, or blank if the patients row is missing. Must correctly identify that this preserves appointments rows even without a match (RIGHT JOIN), not the reverse.

query: SELECT name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id);
gold_checklist: Must say: name of customers that have at least one related row in orders. Must not describe this as returning combined columns from both tables — EXISTS only checks presence, it doesn't pull data from orders.

query: SELECT b.id, b.price, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY b.genre ORDER BY b.price DESC) AS rnk FROM books b;
gold_checklist: Must say: ranks books by price WITHIN each genre group (not company/table-wide), highest price = rank 1 in each group. Must explicitly mention the per-genre partitioning.

query: SELECT AVG(age) AS average_age FROM patients;
gold_checklist: Must say: the average age across all rows of patients — a single number, not a per-row or per-group result.

query: SELECT c.id, c.email, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.country ORDER BY c.email DESC) AS rnk FROM customers c;
gold_checklist: Must say: ranks customers by email WITHIN each country group (not company/table-wide), highest email = rank 1 in each group. Must explicitly mention the per-country partitioning.

query: SELECT AVG(email) AS average_email FROM customers;
gold_checklist: Must say: the average email across all rows of customers — a single number, not a per-row or per-group result.

query: SELECT * FROM accounts ORDER BY opened_date DESC LIMIT 5;
gold_checklist: Must say: the 5 most recent accounts by opened_date, all columns, newest first. Must mention both the limit of 5 and the descending order.

query: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
gold_checklist: Must say: name of employees whose salary is above the average salary of ALL employees. Must reflect the average is computed across the whole table, not a filtered subset.

query: SELECT a1.title AS person, a2.title AS related_person FROM books a1 JOIN books a2 ON a1.id = a2.id - 1;
gold_checklist: Must say: pairs each row of books with the row whose id is exactly one less, showing both titles side by side (a self-join, comparing books against itself, not against a different table).
